assumptions.theory: Einstein GR, Lambda=0 local isolated approximation; no extra fields
assumptions.source: Nonrelativistic baryonic rest-mass density; pressure, mass-current and nonlinear metric terms not computed
assumptions.boundary: Regular field away from the central cusp, isolated potential tending to zero at infinity; no imposed incoming radiation
assumptions.dynamics: Slow test particles: d2x/dt2=-grad(Phi), leading Newtonian order of GR, not a full geodesic/Einstein solver
assumptions.lensing: Born approximation, line of sight along z, face-on disk; physical deflection at infinity, not image positions, shear or an observed lens
assumptions.comparison: Additional material NFW halo from existing models.js; not an emergent vacuum solution
assumptions.excluded: No self-gravitating particle evolution, backreaction, equilibrium/stability certification or full 1PN solution

sources.name: Carroll (1997), cap. 6: equações linearizadas e campo fraco
Lasenby, Hobson e Barker (2023): revisão crítica do gravitomagnetismo galáctico
Cooperstock e Tieu (2005): proposta de interpretação relativística
Korzyński (2005): fonte singular na proposta acima
BIPM: velocidade da luz exata no SI

parameters.particleSoftening: Not applied: unsoftened continuous analytical profiles; not compared directly to a softened live snapshot

vacuum.scope: Exact spherical vacuum control for a hypothetical compact central mass, not the extended Hernquist+Miyamoto-Nagai galaxy. Local speed measured by a static observer, areal radius.

convergence.interpretation: Second-order KDK suggests ratio approaching 4 in its asymptotic regime; this measured ratio is not an equilibrium criterion or an exact GR accuracy certificate.

conclusion: No additional halo-like field has been derived from baryons in this leading-order isolated GR calculation. No full nonlinear Einstein solution or galaxy equilibrium has been certified.
